summary: Correct, minimal bug fix: the MiniMax M2 arg converter was calling str.strip() on each parameter value, silently deleting leading/trailing whitespace that is part of the argument data (e.g. indented code or newline-terminated content passed to an exact-match edit tool). Removing the strip preserves the value verbatim, matching the glm47 converter, and is well covered by new tests.
actions_taken: Read the diff: vllm/parser/minimax_m2.py (dropped .strip() on match.group('value') in both the complete-match and partial-match loops of _minimax_m2_arg_converter) and its new tests in tests/tool_parsers/test_minimax_m2_tool_parser.py.

Traced whether streaming and non-streaming could diverge on whitespace (the classic parser regression): both paths route through the same self._arg_converter in vllm/parser/engine/parser_engine.py -- streaming via _compute_arg_delta (line ~946) and _flush_arg_converter (line ~982), non-streaming via _build_extracted_result (line ~1031). Fixing the single shared converter keeps both paths in agreement by construction; the name is still stripped, which is correct.

Confirmed the comment's consistency claim: vllm/parser/glm47_moe.py's _glm47_arg_converter (lines 60/68) likewise keeps match.group('value') verbatim and only strips the key, so this change aligns minimax_m2 with the existing glm47 behavior.

Verified the new tests fail-without/pass-with logic: pre-fix the converter would have returned {'msg': 'hello world'} (stripped) instead of {'msg': ' hello world '}, so the tests exercise the actual fix and assert observable output through the converter and the streaming public API.
Ran the full file: pytest tests/tool_parsers/test_minimax_m2_tool_parser.py -q -p no:cacheprovider -> 24 passed (no existing tests regressed by preserving whitespace).
